appraisal_events.evidence: on parlait dans les journaux avec les plus grands éloges de son admirable conduite et il était question de la décorer... 'je n'ai qu'une seule qualité, je ne suis pas lâche... c'est grâce à cette résolution que j'ai pu sauver à peu près le château'
appraisal_events.explanation: The press publicly celebrates Gilberte's wartime conduct at Tansonville and floats a decoration, but the narrator quietly notes that this heroic version contradicts the frightened account she gave in her earlier letter, casting the elevation in an ironic light.

appraisal_events.evidence: je l'avais approché avec ce sentiment de timidité... il avait encore au front une cicatrice plus auguste et plus mystérieuse pour moi que l'empreinte laissée sur la terre par le pied d'un géant.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator receives the returning Saint-Loup with reverence and a sense of the sacred, marked by an almost mythic aura of survival and combat that elevates him above ordinary men.

status_effects.explanation: Newspapers praise her conduct at Tansonville and a decoration is discussed, publicly elevating her standing, even as the narrator flags the story's inconsistency with her own earlier account.
The narrator regards him with awe as a marked survivor of the front, investing him with a mysterious, almost sacred stature.

ambiguities: Gilberte's heroic account of remaining at Tansonville to defend it contradicts her earlier 1914 letter describing a frightened flight from the Germans; the narrator notes but does not resolve this discrepancy, so her praised conduct is presented with an ironic undertone.
